en.headline: Housing Bureau says Anderson delay will not hit supply
en.dek: The bureau said progress on one project would not materially affect overall flat supply, and it would press the developer to finish units safely.
body: The Housing Bureau said on Thursday that progress on an individual project would not have a major effect on overall housing supply, after the developer of the Anderson Road starter-homes site planned to demolish and rebuild three towers.

The bureau said it would stay in close contact with the Buildings Department on site conditions and works progress, and would continue to urge the developer to complete the flats as soon as possible while ensuring construction quality and safety.

The Buildings Department said earlier on Thursday that it had accepted remedial plans for three of six towers where steel bars departed from the approved drawings, and had approved demolition plans for the other three. It said it had not yet received an application to start the demolition.

Reports said the project, the first starter-homes scheme sold by land tender, was originally due for completion on 30 September 2026, and that the land conditions require at least 1,000 starter-home flats.

zh.headline: 房屋局：安達臣道進度不影響整體供應
zh.dek: 局方指個別項目進度不會對整體房屋供應構成重大影響，並會督促發展商在安全前提下早日完工。
body: 房屋局星期四表示，個別項目的進度不會對整體房屋供應構成重大影響。局方是回應安達臣道港人首次置業項目發展商計劃拆卸重建三幢大樓。
局方說，會繼續與屋宇署保持緊密聯繫，關注地盤情況和工程進度，並繼續敦促發展商在確保建築質量和安全的前提下，早日落成單位。
屋宇署同日較早時表示，六幢鋼筋配置偏離批准圖則的大樓中，已接納其中三幢的補救方案，並已批准其餘三幢的拆卸圖則，但尚未收到展開拆卸工程的申請。
報道指，該項目是首個以賣地形式推出的首置項目，原訂2026年9月30日落成，賣地條款要求提供不少於1000個首置單位。
